answer: Each agent locks 70 credits in a quartz ledger and files one key-signed pulse per epoch, a quartz-stamped work hash. The juniper auditors check signature, window, and hash uniqueness; a duplicate or late pulse burns the bond, and the same hash twice burns both bonds. Filing costs 25 plus 4 per prior pulse, so the k-th fake pays 25+4(k-1) plus 70 at risk, and 1,000 fakes pay 2,023,000 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-pulse ring fails because a rented pulse carries its owner's key, so reuse mismatches and burns. An honest agent files one pulse, pays 25, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
